method: Reopened the dated faculty rules and assessment annex, checked the cohort-specific requirements, then reconsidered the workbook contributions and tested the repaired schedules before inspecting the finished exception.
findings: Part B specifies two language-specific tracks. The umbrella case uses the first-listed Dutch track under the neutral tie-break. It explicitly specifies the 60/60/60 pathway for September 2026, including two restricted faculty-wide slots and an open 30 EC minor. It requires research workshops in two Dutch Studies areas. Article 7.1 prescribes 50 first-year EC, 100 overall and Research Approaches for thesis entry. The generic assessment annex retains legacy course names and a different threshold and does not displace the adopted cohort-specific rule.

The UCR Dutch course teaches introductory clause order, pronunciation and cultural practices. Psycholinguistics teaches experimental acquisition and processing, and Style & Meaning contributes linguistic analysis. Advanced literary interpretation and comparative historical works give real depth in methods. The trials still lack the Dutch-language historical and modern corpus and cumulative study of Dutch usage that organise the selected track. Frisian studies likewise centre on a distinct linguistic and literary tradition. UCR work on bilingualism and Indigenous cultural continuity supports comparison at the level of themes without establishing a sustained Frisian or minority-language study pathway. Neither the absence of a degree title nor the timetable conflict determines the outcome.
All three trials are feasible under the active workbook. The external-only record presents the 22 verified components with their restricted or open choices, workshop breadth and thesis-entry note.
